prize_parts.citation: for establishing biomolecular phase separation as a physical-chemical principle of intracellular organization

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen for biomolecular phase separation. The achievement is a general thermodynamic statement about cells. Multivalent, weak interactions produce demixing governed by saturation concentrations and phase diagrams, and the 2009 P-granule work and the Rosen multivalency reconstitutions are the least contested demonstrations of it, reproduced across many laboratories and in vitro systems. It has changed how chemists describe cellular interiors and now informs aggregation disease, synthetic compartments and drug partitioning. I take the round-1 exchange to show that this is the shortlisted candidate with the clearest new concept of molecular organisation, and the only physical-chemical one among the leading ballots. The remaining question is whether that conceptual strength is enough on its own to carry a vote this year.
statement.case_against: I have to be honest that the round-1 exchange has not helped the maturity argument. Aili, Linke and Aqvist rank it third, fifth and seventh, and nobody beyond me puts it in a preferred configuration, so on the record it is far from five votes. The physiological extent of liquid-liquid phase separation remains contested, some in-cell claims rest on overexpression or imaging artefacts, and Pappu and Mittag's sequence grammar is real theory that a three-name cut leaves out. The degradation candidacy has broader backing and more visible downstream impact, and I do not think the committee should treat my enthusiasm as a substitute for that. If the debate over cellular generality has not narrowed by the next cycle I would not insist on this one.

responses.point: Linke asked what measurement would settle whether the principle of phase separation is general, and noted that three names are tight given Pappu and Mittag.
responses.response: The decisive test is not a single measurement but concordance: a measured saturation concentration in the cell that matches the in vitro value, a sharp threshold response to concentration changes at fixed composition, and material properties (fusion, wetting, internal mobility) that fit a liquid. Those hold for P granules and nucleoli, which are the systems the three named laureates established. They are much less well established for many of the later claims, and I accept that this limits generality. On credit, Pappu and Mittag built the sequence-encoded theory on top of that foundation; I would still cite the founding demonstrations, but I accept this is the weakest point of my configuration and I will not argue that the cut is free of cost.

responses.point: Aili ranked condensates third and would support revisiting them in a few years when the debate over physiological relevance has narrowed.
responses.response: I agree that timing is the live argument, and our fields overlap enough that I recognise the over-reading of in vitro droplets you describe. I would keep the distinction I drew before: the debate concerns how much of the cell is organised this way, not whether multivalent demixing happens, which is a physical-chemical fact. Where I move toward you is on what the committee can defend this year. If the vote shows that condensates cannot reach a majority, I would rather support a degradation prize with a tightly worded citation than split votes, and I would see a later condensates prize as a better-prepared one.

responses.point: Chabes argued that the cytosine editor and the adenine editor are separate chemical achievements, the latter requiring evolution of TadA to act on DNA, and that Komor and Gaudelli should be credited alongside Liu.
responses.response: This sharpens my round-1 view and I should correct it. I called base editing an engineering of a known reaction, but evolving a tRNA adenosine deaminase to act on DNA has no natural counterpart, and that is real chemistry in the enzymatic sense. My remaining concern is the one you share: the 2020 proximity and the Kondo/Nishida attribution gap. I would keep B061 as an alternative rather than dismiss it, and if the committee goes there I would favour Liu, Komor and Gaudelli over Liu alone.

responses.point: Somfai argued that Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is the cleanest case on attribution and maturity, as a two-person prize of Buchwald and Hartwig, and that the 2010 prize did not cover amination.
responses.response: I agree the attribution is clean and the maturity is unquestionable, and I take the point that the 2010 prize did not recognise amination. As a physical chemist I am less able to judge the ligand-design and reductive-elimination arguments than you or Zou, so I defer on the mechanistic distinction. My reluctance is only about balance: a synthetic-method prize would leave soft-matter and physical-chemical concepts unrepresented in a year when the other leading ballots are all chemical biology. I do not regard that as a scientific objection to B008.

responses.point: Brzezinski argued that the cereblon molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray) is arguably the more decisive insight and cannot fit within a three-name PROTAC prize.
responses.response: I agree this is the main structural problem for B028 and I do not think three names can honestly cover both strands. It is the reason I list B028 as an alternative and not as my preferred part: it would need a citation limited to the PROTAC design principle, and the committee should say openly that the glue strand is left out. I take your point that this is a statement about the field and not a flaw in the science.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that the physiological extent of liquid-liquid phase separation is settled enough for a prize now, given that I cannot point to votes beyond my own.
Whether a three-name cut without Pappu and Mittag is defensible, or whether the founding-demonstration trio should be preferred over a broader attribution.
Whether a B028 citation limited to the PROTAC design principle is acceptable when the cereblon glue strand is left out.
Whether base editing follows too closely on the 2020 prize, and whether Komor and Gaudelli should be credited.
statement.conflict_note: No recusal-level conflict. I have no personal or institutional tie to Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu or Mittag. My research on lipid-protein co-assembly and amyloid is scientifically adjacent to condensates, and I share Lund affiliation with Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, which I flag for transparency only. Chair summary notes confirm no recusal was requested.
